arxiv-2505-09603.text:
• Problem: generalist robot policies underperform on specific tasks; naively co-training with large prior datasets can hurt performance.
• Key idea: DataMIL uses datamodels to select prior data by its estimated effect on policy performance, not similarity.
• Proxy metric: held-out target-demo behavior cloning loss replaces costly rollouts, making selection offline and differentiable.
• Estimators: regression datamodels for small MLP policies; metagradient-based estimator scales to Octo transformer diffusion policies.
• Robotics tweaks: cluster samples into sub-trajectories or trajectories, and mix half the target data to reduce distribution shift.
• Results: MetaWorld 50 tasks ~10% over baselines; LIBERO-10 37.8% average, best overall; OXE real-world 61.0% vs 40.0% best baseline.
• What's new: offline, performance-aware selection from heterogeneous OXE, including the unseen Tiago embodiment and multitask Droid targets.

arxiv-2611-05368.text:
• Problem: robot teleop data collection is unguided; post-hoc curation wastes effort already spent on uninformative demos.
• Key idea: GUILD decides what data to collect next, optimizing downstream performance in an inaccessible deployment environment.
• Method: VLM (GPT-5.2) proposes scenes, object configs, tasks; MAGIC metagradient attribution scores each task's marginal utility.
• Closed loop: collect batches on highest-utility task; VLM expands task set using utility-ranked feedback.
• Setup: Octo policy co-trained with few target demos; LIBERO-90 (16 training scenes) and 6 real kitchens/bathrooms/offices.
• Results: matches or beats FSC, STRAP, VLM-Uniform, Random; ~25% over VLM-Uniform in real open-world; beats All-Data.
• Also beats average of 8 roboticists in LIBERO and 2 real-world experts; cheaper than FSC (one policy).

arxiv-2506-15847.text:
• Problem: robots learning multi-step mobile manipulation from one third-person human video, safely and without human supervision.
• Key idea: adapt parsed human actions via real-world exploration filtered by simulation-pretrained safety Q-function ensembles.
• Parsing: body/hand tracking, contact detection and GPT-4o segment videos into semantic goals plus egocentric motions.
• Exploration samples actions around human motion, rejects predicted failures, backtracks, and switches grasp modes when stuck.
• Setup: Tiago++ robot, seven household tasks, safety Q-functions trained on OmniGibson point clouds for six failure types.
• Results: at least 40% task success vs 0% direct execution; unsafe actions 0.6% vs 14.2% without safety Q-functions.
• New: grasp-mode adaptation was needed in 6/7 tasks; policy memory cuts later exploration up to 67%.

arxiv-2611-06881.text:
• Problem: industrial robots need reliable performance on fixed tasks with structured object and pose variations, called Variational Automation.
• Existing benchmarks like LIBERO and ManiSkill are saturating and focus on household pick-and-place, not automation.
• VABAR: open simulation benchmark with six tasks: tool sorting, tool hanging, gear meshing, syringe packing, cable insertion, cable routing.
• Setup: Franka and bimanual YAM robots, Newton physics plus Isaac Lab Arena, two difficulty levels, 30 instances each.
• Provides 55+ assets, 33 reusable skills, human-authored reference solutions, and execution records for diagnosing failures.
• Results: GaP beats Claude Code in 11/12 conditions (gear meshing 70% vs 0%) but trails human graphs.
• Motion planning causes most failures; USB-C insertion drops from 86.7% to 30% with human graphs at Level 2.

pdf-beb8536dd7.text:
• FDA CDRH discussion paper (Nov 2026) seeking feedback on benefit-risk of autonomous and remotely teleoperated robotic devices.
• Not guidance or policy; feeds a December 2-3, 2026 public workshop and public docket comments.
• Proposes shared terms: robotic device system, user, autonomy, levels of autonomy, remote teleoperation.
• Distinguishes autonomy (adaptive planning) from automaticity; compares Yang's six levels with IEC 60601-4-1, Haidegger, and Schmidgall.
• Autonomy risks: errors outpacing intervention, automation bias, AI opacity, data shift, slow control handoff.
• Teleoperation risks: latency, connectivity loss, lost sensory cues, adverse-event management, and local backup staffing.
• No numerical results; no remote or fully autonomous systems authorized as of July 2026; poses 15 questions.

pdf-556e228a43.text:
• Problem: value-based offline RL for multi-turn LLM/VLM tasks scales poorly and discards pretrained likelihoods via new value heads.
• Key idea: Q-SFT learns Q-values directly as token probabilities using a weighted cross-entropy, SFT-like objective.
• Method: Bellman targets weight the log-likelihood; policy at inference ∝ behavior policy × exp(β·learned probability).
• Theory: learned probabilities are conservative Q estimates, bounded between πβ·Q* and Q* for non-negligible actions.
• Setup: GPT2-medium, LLaVA-1.6, RT-1-style transformer; chess, Wordle, 20Q, WebShop, ALFWorld, robotic manipulation.
• Results: WebShop 0.63 vs ReAct 0.60; robot pick 94% vs QT 92%, CQL 78%, BC 44%.
• New: no architecture changes needed; learns faster than QT and benefits more from larger pretrained models than ILQL.

arxiv-2410-24164.text:
• Problem: generalist robot policies need data scale, dexterity, and robustness beyond narrow task-specific imitation learning.
• Key idea: π0 adds a flow-matching "action expert" to pre-trained PaliGemma VLM, yielding 3.3B-parameter VLA.
• Method: 50-step action chunks via flow matching, 10 Euler steps, up to 50 Hz control, ~73 ms inference.
• Setup: pre-trained on ~10,000 hours, 7 robot configurations, 68 tasks, plus OXE, then task-specific post-training.
• Out-of-box: near-perfect shirt folding and easy bussing, far exceeding OpenVLA and Octo, even at compute parity.
• Fine-tuning: beats ACT, Diffusion Policy, OpenVLA, Octo; pre-training sometimes gives 2x gains over scratch training.
• New: long multi-stage tasks like laundry, box building, and egg packing, scoring above 50% on every task.

arxiv-2511-14759.text:
• Problem: imitation-trained VLAs plateau at demo quality and compound errors; real-world RL for large flow-based VLAs is hard.
• Key idea: RECAP extracts policies by conditioning on a binarized advantage indicator, avoiding policy gradients and log-likelihoods.
• Method: a distributional value function predicts steps-to-success; actions above a per-task advantage threshold are labeled "Advantage: positive".
• Data: demos, autonomous rollouts, and human corrections forced positive; iterated offline RL, retraining from the pretrained checkpoint.
• Setup: π*0.6 (Gemma 3 4B, 860M action expert) offline-RL pretrained, then fine-tuned on bimanual 6-DoF arms.
• Results: throughput more than doubles and failures roughly halve on diverse laundry and espresso; ~90%+ success on most tasks.
• Also: beats AWR and PPO, gives 97% success on targeted failure removal, and ran espresso for 13 hours straight.

arxiv-2512-22414.text:
• Problem: VLAs need diverse data; human videos are scalable but hard to use without hand-engineered human-robot alignment.
• Key idea: human-to-robot transfer emerges once VLA pretraining spans enough scenes, tasks, and embodiments.
• Method: treat humans as another embodiment; co-finetune π0.5 on 3D hand-track actions plus subtask language, no alignment.
• Setup: head and wrist cameras, 14 hours of human data, 50-50 mix with nearest robot task, four generalization tasks.
• Results: Spice 32→71%, Dresser 25→50%, Bussing 53→63%, egg sorting accuracy 57→78%; average score nearly doubles.
• Scaling: no gain at 0–25% pretraining diversity; largest gains with 100% plus cross-embodiment data.
• Insight: t-SNE shows human and robot latents converge with diverse pretraining; human data rivals target robot data on two tasks.

arxiv-2504-16054.text:
• Problem: VLAs rarely generalize beyond training scenes; long-horizon household tasks in unseen homes remain unsolved.
• Key idea: co-train one VLA on heterogeneous data: multi-robot, web, subtask prediction, verbal instructions, object detection.
• Method: same model predicts subtask text, then continuous actions via 300M flow-matching action expert on PaliGemma.
• Training: FAST-token pre-training 280k steps, then 80k post-training steps adding flow matching; 97.6% non-mobile-manipulator data.
• Setup: two 18-19 DoF bimanual mobile manipulators, ~400h data from ~100 homes, tested in unseen homes.
• Results: 104 training homes match in-test-home baseline; removing ME/CE drops ~78% to ~50%; π0.5 beats π0.
• New: first end-to-end system cleaning kitchens and bedrooms in new homes, 10-15 minute tasks.

arxiv-2604-15483.text:
• Problem: VLAs struggle to compose skills, follow novel instructions, and match task-specific fine-tuned models without per-task fine-tuning.
• Key idea: condition training on rich context: subtask language, subgoal images, episode metadata (speed, quality, mistakes), control mode.
• Method: 5B VLA (Gemma3 4B, MEM memory, 860M flow action expert); BAGEL-14B world model generates subgoals.
• Data: demos, failures, RL/autonomous eval rollouts, egocentric human video, web data; prompt dropout plus metadata CFG.
• Results: matches RL-finetuned π*0.6 specialists out-of-box on espresso, laundry, box building, with higher throughput on two.
• Zero-shot UR5e shirt folding: 85.6% progress, 80% success vs expert human teleoperators' 90.9%, 80.6%.
• New: language coaching teaches unseen tasks (air fryer, bagel); metadata lets performance improve with lower-quality data.

arxiv-2501-09747.text:
• Problem: per-dimension, per-timestep binning tokenization makes autoregressive VLAs fail on high-frequency, dexterous robot data.
• Cause: highly correlated consecutive tokens carry little marginal information, so next-token prediction degenerates into copying.
• Key idea FAST: compress action chunks with DCT, quantize coefficients, then byte-pair encode into dense tokens.
• FAST+: universal tokenizer trained on 1M action chunks, released as a HuggingFace AutoProcessor.
• Setup: π0 (PaliGemma-3B) and OpenVLA backbones, tested on 6 real-robot tasks plus the LIBERO simulation benchmark.
• Results: up to 13x fewer tokens (700→53); naive fails on 20–50Hz tasks while FAST succeeds; beats FSQ.
• π0-FAST matches diffusion π0 on 10k hours of data with 5x less training compute; enables zero-shot DROID policy.

arxiv-2604-23073.text:
• Problem: VLAs generalize broadly but are slow and imprecise in the "last millimeter" of contact-rich tasks.
• Key idea: VLA exposes a compact "RL token" via encoder-decoder bottleneck, enabling lightweight sample-efficient online RL.
• Method: small off-policy actor-critic over action chunks (C=10), conditioned on and regularized toward VLA reference actions.
• Tricks: reference-action dropout prevents copying; high update-to-data ratio; RL applied only to human-selected critical phases.
• Setup: π0.6 VLA, four real tasks: screw installation, zip tie fastening, Ethernet and charger insertion, 50 Hz control.
• Results: up to 3× faster critical phases; screw success 20%→65%; full-task gains +40% screw, +60% zip tie.
• New: beats HIL-SERL, PLD, DSRL, DAgger; Ethernet median 66 steps versus 146 for expert teleoperation.
